summary.headline: Punjab & Sind Bank Q2 FY27: business up 15.73% to Rs.2,79,231 crore, advances up 19.28%, net profit up nearly 40% to Rs.412 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported business growth of 15.73% to Rs.2,79,231 crore, with deposits up 12.97% to Rs.1,53,312 crore and advances up 19.28% to Rs.1,25,919 crore. Operating profit rose 22% YoY to Rs.617 crore and net profit rose nearly 40% to Rs.412 crore, helped by 23.6% growth in core fee income and net interest income up 22%. Asset quality improved, with gross NPA at 2.09% and net NPA at 0.61%. Management said treasury performance was muted due to hardening yields and geopolitical factors, and flagged slower co-lending and a planned Rs.7,000 crore capital raise via QIP.

financial_highlights.change: CASA up 7.5% YoY but share declined

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 42% YoY; RAM (retail, agri, MSME) advances rose over 31%, taking RAM share of gross advances to 61.37% from 55.15% a year earlier.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 28.69% YoY; MSME digital lending limit raised to Rs.3 crore from Rs.1 crore.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate credit pipeline of about Rs.20,000 crore (Rs.12,000 crore pipeline plus Rs.8,000-9,000 crore in-principle sanctions); management plans to shrink corporate share over time.

guidance_outlook: Deposit growth guided at 13%-14% and advances growth at 18%-20%; CD ratio expected around 82% over the next two quarters.
RAM share of advances guided at about 65% for the current year and 70% by March 2028 (management also cited March 2027 for 65%).
Gross NPA expected below 2% by end-March; net NPA guidance 0.65%, already at 0.61%.
Recovery and upgradation guidance of Rs.1,000 crore-plus; Rs.622 crore achieved so far.
Business target of Rs.3 lakh crore by end of FY27 and Rs.4 lakh crore by FY29, with possible earlier achievement.
ECL transition: additional provisioning of about 5% of net worth (around Rs.700 crore) with a glide path; steady-state credit cost of 0.5%-0.6%; RWA changes from 1 April 2027.
capex_capacity: Capital raise: Rs.7,000 crore additional funding done this quarter; merchant bankers appointed and QIP is the primary route, timing dependent on market.
GIFT City branch expected to go live around end-November 2026.
Forex trade module expected to go live in Q3 FY27; supply chain finance system live with two to three corporates.
Branch expansion: top 200 districts identified (80% of banking business); 300 potential centres found; branches to open as premises and staff are finalised.

Cybersecurity upgrade RFP targeted to complete this quarter; Resilience Operations Centre first phase by December 2026 and full by March 2027; recovery management tool in 6-9 months (phase one by March).
demand_pricing: Digital lending: over 50% of vehicle loans and over 40% of housing loans processed digitally/STP/assisted; about 40,000 proposals worth about Rs.8,000 crore sourced digitally since 4 November 2024, with sanction rates of about 50% (vehicle) and 40% (home).
Gold loan ceiling raised to Rs.50 lakh from Rs.2.5 lakh.
Co-lending has slowed pending integration work on RBI CLM-1 and CLM-2 guidelines; management expects 1-2 months to complete integration.
Treasury constrained by hardening yields; management expects some NIM support from the 25 bps rate hike and further hikes.
Technically written-off (TWO) book about Rs.7,344 crore; Rs.247.88 crore recovered so far this year, versus about 10% annual recovery in recent years.
SMA ratio fell from above 9% to below 4%; target 2%-2.5% in a short span.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked what drives the upward guidance and what initiatives support credit growth, RAM breakup, and treasury outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Management retained business guidance and said NPA targets could be exceeded; cited digital platforms (12 products on a single QR code), HR transformation, and branch expansion. Treasury is constrained, but management expects margins to improve with rate hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about corporate book visibility, digital spend, and supply chain and co-lending.
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate pipeline of about Rs.20,000 crore built over the last year or two; supply chain system is live with two to three corporates; co-lending has slowed pending RBI-compliant integration, expected in one to two months. Specific digital and HR spend figures were not given.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the chatter on PSB consolidation and the high-level banking reform committee.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it had no information on consolidation and that the committee had not yet been formed as far as the bank understood; the government decides.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the ECL transition impact and steady-state credit cost from FY28.
qa_highlights.answer: CRO said the additional impact is about 5% of net worth (around Rs.700 crore), including HTM MTM, with a glide path making CRAR impact negligible; steady-state provisioning of 0.5%-0.6%. SMA 1+2 standard-asset credit cost was not available and will be shared separately.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked whether the bank will change the corporate vs RAM mix and whether it is active in mid-sized corporates.
qa_highlights.answer: Strategy is to keep increasing RAM share to 65% by March 2027 and about 70% by March 2028; corporate churn continues on pricing, and MSMEs will be supported if pricing is competitive.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about capital raising plans given ECL impact and CD ratio.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said optimum CD ratio of 82%-83% is achievable; Rs.7,000 crore raised for capital, approvals obtained, and QIP is the preferred route, timing subject to market conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the TWO book, recovery, technology roadmap, and DPDP/cyber readiness.
qa_highlights.answer: TWO book about Rs.7,344 crore with Rs.247.88 crore recovered so far; recovery tool vendor appointed. Cybersecurity RFP targeted this quarter and Resilience Operations Centre phased by December and March.

risks_watch: Gross NPA trajectory against the below-2% target and SMA progress toward 2%-2.5%.
ECL transition: about Rs.700 crore net worth hit, possible additional HTM mark-to-market impact if yields rise further, and Stage 2 management.
CASA ratio slipped to 28.83% despite 7.5% YoY growth; deposit growth must hit 13%-14% to support the CD ratio.
Capital raise timing (Rs.7,000 crore QIP) amid weak market conditions, as one analyst noted.
Co-lending restart after RBI CLM integration; corporate pipeline pricing discipline.
Treasury income remains muted with hardening yields; NIM expansion depends on rate moves.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating and asset-quality delivery and on guidance, with the CEO saying NPA targets could be exceeded. Cautious on treasury and yields, and evasive on consolidation, the banking reform committee, and the SMA 1+2 credit cost, which was deferred to a separate reply.
key_quotes: So overall, we expect that the CD ratio will be around 82 % over the next two quarters.
We continue to expect the gross NPA to be below 2% by the end of March.
The co -lending as of now seems to have slowed down a bit.
So, the Resilience Operations Centre is getting implemented. By December, it will have the first phase of implementation.

adds.what: Branch expansion across top 200 districts (300 potential centres identified; branches to open as premises and staff are finalised)

growth.why: Advances guided at 18%-20% and deposits at 13%-14% for FY27 with Rs.3 lakh crore business target; backing is a Rs.20,000 crore corporate pipeline, digital lending and retail momentum (retail advances +42%), plus a GIFT City branch due around end-November 2026 and branch rollout, but no quantified capacity or order timing beyond that.
